why: Sleep can influence pain sensitivity, energy, mood, and your ability to participate in recovery.

slides.title: Sleep & Healing
slides.content: Sleep supports many recovery processes and can affect how sensitive, rested, and capable you feel the next day.

slides.title: Make Room for Sleep
slides.content: Most adults are advised to get at least 7 hours regularly, although individual needs and circumstances vary.

slides.title: Sleep Hygiene Basics
slides.content: A reasonably consistent schedule, a comfortable environment, and a wind-down routine can support sleep. Choose changes that are realistic for you.

slides.title: Sleep Is More Than Hours
slides.content: Timing, regularity, continuity, and how rested you feel can all matter—not only the number on the clock.

slides.title: Avoid the Perfect-Sleep Trap
slides.content: One difficult night does not ruin recovery. Look for patterns over time and focus on changes you can sustain.

slides.title: Try this tonight
slides.content: Choose one experiment tonight: dim the lights, reduce stimulating content, or give yourself a consistent wind-down period. Notice what helps.
